claim: A method for in-focus data acquisition with a phase plate enables near-atomic resolution single particle reconstructions.
source: We present a method for in-focus data acquisition with a phase plate that enables near-atomic resolution single particle reconstructions.
evidence: The abstract states this as a primary finding, and the manuscript demonstrates this with experimental data showing 3.2 Å resolution reconstruction.

claim: Accurate focusing is the determining factor for obtaining high quality data with phase plates.
source: Accurate focusing is the determining factor for obtaining high quality data.
evidence: The manuscript demonstrates through experimental results that implementing precise focusing improved resolution from ~8Å to 3.2Å.

claim: A double-area focusing strategy achieves the required precision for in-focus phase plate data acquisition.
source: A double-area focusing strategy was implemented in order to achieve the required precision.
evidence: The manuscript describes the implementation and demonstrates improved results with this approach.

claim: A 3.2 Å resolution reconstruction of the Thermoplasma acidophilum 20S proteasome was obtained using the Volta phase plate.
source: With this approach we obtained a 3.2 Å resolution reconstruction of the Thermoplasma acidophilum 20S proteasome.
evidence: The manuscript presents experimental data and FSC curves demonstrating this resolution.

claim: The phase plate matches or slightly exceeds the performance of the conventional defocus approach.
source: The phase plate matches or slightly exceeds the performance of the conventional defocus approach.
evidence: Figure 6A shows comparable resolution versus number of particles for VPP and CTEM datasets.

claim: Spherical aberration becomes a limiting factor for achieving resolutions below 3 Å with in-focus phase plate images.
source: Spherical aberration becomes a limiting factor for achieving resolutions below 3 Å with in-focus phase plate images.
evidence: Figure 1B shows theoretical calculations demonstrating a resolution cutoff at about 2.7 Å due to spherical aberration.

claim: The phase plate could enable single particle analysis of challenging samples in terms of small size, heterogeneity and flexibility that are difficult to solve by the conventional defocus approach.
source: The phase plate could enable single particle analysis of challenging samples in terms of small size, heterogeneity and flexibility that are difficult to solve by the conventional defocus approach.
evidence: This is a speculative statement about future applications based on the improved contrast properties demonstrated.

claim: Direct electron detectors changed the prospects of the cryo-EM field with atomic resolution structures becoming almost routine.
source: Direct electron detectors already changed the prospects of the cryo-EM field (Henderson, 2015) with atomic resolution structures becoming almost routine (Campbell et al., 2015; Bartesaghi et al., 2015).
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to published literature.

claim: Phase plates improve the image contrast and allow in-focus data acquisition which will result in increase of the signal-to-noise ratio across the entire frequency spectrum.
source: Phase plates improve the image contrast and allow in-focus data acquisition which, in theory, will result in increase of the signal-to-noise ratio across the entire frequency spectrum (Glaeser, 2013).
evidence: This theoretical expectation is supported by a citation and demonstrated in the manuscript's images.

claim: Various practical problems and performance issues have prevented the acquisition of high-resolution datasets with a phase plate until now.
source: Until now, however, various practical problems and performance issues have prevented the acquisition of high-resolution datasets with a phase plate (Danev et al., 2009).
evidence: This is supported by citation and the authors' own previous work showing limited resolution.

claim: With correct use, in particular accurate focusing, one can achieve near-atomic resolutions with phase plates.
source: Here we demonstrate that with correct use, in particular accurate focusing, one can achieve near-atomic resolutions.
evidence: This is demonstrated by the experimental data showing 3.2 Å resolution.

claim: The phase plate produces phase contrast by introducing a phase shift between the scattered and unscattered waves at a diffraction plane inside the microscope.
source: The phase plate is a device that produces phase contrast by introducing a phase shift between the scattered and unscattered waves at a diffraction plane inside the microscope.
evidence: This is an established principle of phase plate operation.

claim: Phase contrast denotes that phase variations of the electron wave caused by the sample will be transformed into amplitude variations at the camera thus enabling phase observation.
source: Phase contrast denotes that phase variations of the electron wave caused by the sample will be transformed into amplitude variations at the camera thus enabling phase observation.
evidence: This is a fundamental principle of phase contrast imaging.

claim: Ideally, the phase shift must be π/2 to realize the so-called Zernike phase contrast.
source: Ideally, the phase shift must be π/2 to realize the so-called Zernike phase contrast (Danev and Nagayama, 2001).
evidence: This is supported by citation to established work on Zernike phase contrast.

claim: A satisfactory phase contrast performance can be obtained within a range of phase shift values (π/4 ~ 3π/4).
source: In practice, however, a satisfactory phase contrast performance can be obtained within a range of phase shift values (π/4 ~ 3π/4) (Danev and Nagayama, 2011).
evidence: This is supported by citation to previous work.

claim: Defocus phase contrast has the disadvantage of low overall contrast because of poor performance at low spatial frequencies.
source: This method is the de facto standard in transmission electron microscopy (TEM) but it has the disadvantage of low overall contrast because of poor performance at low spatial frequencies, i.e. large specimen features are not well reproduced in the image.
evidence: This is established knowledge about defocus phase contrast and is demonstrated in Figure 4.

claim: Phase plates for TEM have been in development for more than 15 years with the thin film Zernike phase being one of the most promising candidates.
source: Phase plates for TEM have been in development for more than 15 years with the thin film Zernike phase being one of the most promising candidates (Glaeser, 2013).
evidence: This is supported by citation and represents historical context.

claim: The thin film Zernike phase plate consists of a thin material film, typically amorphous carbon, with thickness selected for π/2 phase shift at the operating voltage of the microscope (~22 nm for 100 kV; ~31 nm for 300 kV) and a small (~1 μm) hole in the center for the central beam of unscattered electrons.
source: It consists of a thin material film, typically amorphous carbon, with thickness selected for π/2 phase shift at the operating voltage of the microscope (~22 nm for 100 kV; ~31 nm for 300 kV) and a small (~1 μm) hole in the center for the central beam of unscattered electrons (Danev and Nagayama, 2001).
evidence: This is a technical description supported by citation.

claim: The Zernike phase plate has practical issues including a short usable lifespan, produces fringe artifacts in the images, is difficult to use and almost impossible to automate.
source: Nevertheless, the Zrnike phase plate has some practical issues, such as a short usable lifespan, produces fringe artifacts in the images, is difficult to use and almost impossible to automate because the central diffraction beam must be positioned precisely in the middle of the small central hole (Danev et al., 2009).
evidence: This is supported by citation to previous work documenting these issues.

claim: All examples in the literature of single particle analysis with the Zernike phase plate had resolution limited to about one nanometer.
source: There are a few examples in the literature of single particle analysis (SPA) with the Zernike phase plate but in all of them the resolution was limited to about one nanometer (Danev and Nagayama, 2008; Murata et al., 2010).
evidence: This is supported by citations to specific published examples.

claim: The Volta phase plate was developed recently as a successor to the thin film Zernike phase plate.
source: The Volta phase plate (VPP) was developed recently as a successor to the thin film Zernike phase plate (Danev et al., 2014).
evidence: This is supported by citation to the original VPP development paper.

claim: The VPP has a virtually unlimited life, does not produce fringe artifacts and does not require precise centering.
source: It solves most of the issues, in particular, the VPP has a virtually unlimited life, does not produce fringe artifacts and does not require precise centering.
evidence: This is based on the design and operational characteristics of the VPP as described in cited work.

claim: There are application examples of the VPP in cryo-tomography that demonstrate its benefits.
source: There are already a few application examples of the VPP in cryo-tomography (Fukuda et al., 2015; Asano et al., 2015; Mahamid et al., 2016) and single particle analysis (Khoshouei et al., 2016) that demonstrate its benefits.
evidence: This is supported by multiple citations to published applications.

claim: The VPP consists of a thin (~10 nm) continuous amorphous carbon film which is constantly heated to ~200°C to prevent beam-induced contamination.
source: The VPP consists of a thin (~10 nm) continuous amorphous carbon film which is constantly heated to ~200°C to prevent beam-induced contamination.
evidence: This is a technical description of the VPP design supported by citation.

claim: The phase shift in the VPP is created on-the-fly through the interaction of the central diffraction beam with the carbon film.
source: The phase shift is created on-the-fly through the interaction of the central diffraction beam with the carbon film (Danev et al., 2014).
evidence: This describes the operating principle of the VPP, supported by citation.

claim: The only drawback of the VPP is that the phase shift is not constant and increases proportionally to the accumulated dose.
source: This mitigates the requirement for precise centering of the phase plate but also gives rise to the only drawback of the VPP – the phase shift is not constant and increases proportionally to the accumulated dose.
evidence: This is demonstrated in Figure 3 showing phase shift evolution with dose.

claim: The evolving phase shift is not a performance limiting factor but rather a parameter that has to be kept in mind when designing data acquisition strategies.
source: The evolving phase shift is not a performance limiting factor but rather a parameter that has to be kept in mind when designing data acquisition strategies.
evidence: This is an inference based on the successful achievement of high resolution despite the varying phase shift.

claim: A wide open area of the VPP film provides multiple virtual phase plates by just moving from one position to the next.
source: A wide open area of the film provides multiple virtual phase plates by just moving from one position to the next.
evidence: This describes a practical feature of the VPP design.

claim: The distance between VPP positions must be large enough (typically ~20 μm apart) to prevent the previous phase shift spot from interfering with spatial frequencies below the Nyquist frequency of the detector.
source: The distance between the positions must be large enough (typically ~20 μm apart) to prevent the previous phase shift spot from interfering with spatial frequencies below the Nyquist frequency of the detector.
evidence: This is a practical requirement based on the spatial extent of the phase shift effect.

claim: All datasets in this work were collected automatically.
source: All datasets in this work were collected automatically.
evidence: This is a statement about the experimental methodology used.

claim: Initial SPA trials with the VPP were limited to resolutions (~8Å) similar to those already reported with the Zernike phase plate.
source: Our initial SPA trials with the VPP were limited to resolutions (~8A, unpublished data) similar to those already reported with the Zernike phase plate.
evidence: This is based on the authors' unpublished experimental results.

claim: Initial trials used software and data acquisition schemes developed for conventional defocus phase contrast transmission electron microscopy.
source: In those trials we used software and data acquisition schemes developed for conventional defocus phase contrast transmission electron microscopy (CTEM).
evidence: This describes the methodology of the initial experiments.

claim: Conventional CTEM schemes place low priority on focusing accuracy because the defocus is accurately measured by CTF fitting during data processing.
source: Such schemes place low priority on focusing accuracy because with CTEM the defocus is accurately measured by contrast transfer function (CTF) fitting during data processing and some defocus variation is actually desirable and beneficial for the reconstruction (Cheng et al., 2015).
evidence: This is established practice in cryo-EM supported by citation.

claim: Using phase plates in-focus requires very accurate focusing.
source: As shown later, using phase plates in-focus requires very accurate focusing.
evidence: This is demonstrated by the improved results when accurate focusing was implemented.

claim: There are two defocus strategies for SPA data acquisition with a phase plate: collecting data with intentional defocus or collecting data in-focus.
source: In general, there are two defocus strategies for SPA data acquisition with a phase plate. The first one involves collecting data in a similar fashion as in CTEM, i.e. with an intentionally applied defocus... The second and ideal SPA acquisition scheme with a phase plate is to collect data in-focus.
evidence: This describes two possible experimental approaches.

claim: The advantage of the defocused approach with a phase plate is that precise focusing is not required and some defocus variation is actually desirable.
source: The advantage of this approach is that precise focusing in not required and some defocus variation is actually desirable.
evidence: This is an inference based on comparison with CTEM methodology.

claim: The disadvantage of the defocused approach with a phase plate is that the only benefit from using a phase plate is contrast increase for the very low spatial frequencies whereas the remainder of the frequency spectrum has multiple CTF zeroes, like in CTEM.
source: The disadvantage is that the only benefit from using a phase plate is contract increase for the very low spatial frequencies whereas the remainder of the frequency spectrum has multiple CTF zeroes, like in CTEM.
evidence: This is an inference based on CTF theory and phase plate properties.

claim: The advantage of the in-focus approach with a phase plate is that there are no CTF zeroes across the frequency spectrum and there is no need to fit and correct the CTF.
source: The advantage of this approach is that there are no CTF zeroes across the frequency spectrum and there is no need to fit and correct the CTF.
evidence: This is based on CTF theory for in-focus imaging with a phase plate.

claim: The in-focus approach requires very accurate focusing.
source: However, this approach is more demanding on the experiment in that it requires very accurate focusing.
evidence: This is demonstrated by the experimental results showing improved resolution with accurate focusing.

claim: If there are small random defocus errors in the in-focus approach, they cannot be corrected during data processing because fitting the CTF without at least a few detectable CTF zeroes is practically impossible.
source: Also, if there are small random defocus errors they cannot be corrected during data processing because fitting the CTF without at least a few detectable CTF zeroes is practically impossible.
evidence: This is based on the principles of CTF fitting methodology.

claim: Initial SPA trials with the VPP using the defocused approach were not successful, mainly because of the lack of phase shift support in the single particle reconstruction software.
source: In our initial SPA trials with the VPP we also tried the defocused approach but without much success (unpublished data), mainly because of the lack of phase shift support in the single particle reconstruction software.
evidence: This is based on the authors' unpublished experimental results.

claim: The authors have had more success with the in-focus approach than the defocused approach.
source: Future software developments could change the status quo and make the defocused approach more attractive, but so far we have had more success with the in-focus approach (Khoshouei et al., 2016).
evidence: This is based on the authors' experimental results and cited work.

claim: For a π/2 phase plate with 2.7 mm spherical aberration, there is a resolution cutoff at about 2.7 Å for in-focus imaging.
source: For higher resolutions (lower numerical values) the defocus range gets narrower and has a cutoff point at about 2.7 Å.
evidence: This is shown in Figure 1B through theoretical CTF calculations.

claim: Achieving resolutions below 2.7 Å with in-focus phase plate imaging will require reduction or complete elimination of the spherical aberration (Cs correction).
source: Achieving resolutions below that point will require reduction or complete elimination of the spherical aberration (Cs correction).
evidence: This is inferred from the theoretical CTF calculations shown in Figure 1.

claim: The phase shift of the VPP increases with the accumulated dose on the phase plate.
source: The phase shift of the VPP is not constant and increases with the accumulated dose on the phase plate (see Figure 3 below) (Danev et al., 2014, Figure 1).
evidence: This is demonstrated in Figure 3 and supported by citation.

claim: The VPP phase shift has a rapid onset in the beginning followed by a gradual increase.
source: It has a rapid onset in the beginning followed by a gradual increase.
evidence: This is shown in Figure 3 experimental data.

claim: For lower phase shifts, the defocus ranges are shifted towards more defocus and there is a slight improvement in the absolute resolution cutoff point (~2.6 Å).
source: For lower phase shifts (blue area) the defocus ranges are shifted towards more defocus and there is a slight improvement in the absolute resolution cutoff point (~2.6 Å).
evidence: This is shown in Figure 1C through theoretical calculations.

claim: Higher phase shifts require less defocus but have a worse resolution cutoff (~3.0 Å).
source: Higher phase shifts (red area) require less defocus but have a worse resolution cutoff (~3.0 Å).
evidence: This is shown in Figure 1C through theoretical calculations.

claim: With a Cs-corrected microscope (zero spherical aberration) and a π/2 phase plate, there is no resolution cutoff but the allowed defocus range gets progressively narrower for higher resolutions.
source: Figure 1D shows an ideal case of a π/2 phase plate on a Cs-corrected microscope (zero spherical aberration). There is no resolution cutoff but the allowed defocus range gets progressively narrower for higher resolutions.
evidence: This is shown in Figure 1D through theoretical calculations.

claim: Up to 400 nm defocus difference was measured across the two sides (3.0 um distance) of holes on Quantifoil R 1.2/1.3 holey carbon grids.
source: We measured up to 400 nm defocus difference across the two sides (3.0 um distance) of holes on Quantifoil R 1.2/1.3 holey carbon grids.
evidence: This is based on experimental measurements during data acquisition.

claim: A single focusing area acquisition scheme will have a defocus error of up to 200 nm.
source: This would mean that a single focusing area acquisition scheme will have a defocus error of up to 200 nm which is substantial compared to the values in Figure 1.
evidence: This is inferred from the measured 400 nm defocus difference across holes.

claim: A single focusing area scheme with up to 200 nm defocus error provides a plausible explanation for the lower resolution (~8 Å) reconstructions obtained when using a conventional single focusing area scheme.
source: That provides a plausible explanation for the lower resolution (~8 Å) reconstructions we obtained when using a conventional single focusing area scheme.
evidence: This is an inference connecting the focusing error to the observed resolution limitation.

claim: The double area focusing was iterated 2 or 3 times to achieve +/− 10 nm from the target defocus.
source: To improve the accuracy even further the double area focusing was iterated 2 or 3 times depending on how fast it was converging (we typically aimed at +/− 10 nm from the target defocus).
evidence: This describes the experimental methodology used.

claim: The defocus was measured without applying a defocus offset during the measurement to prevent errors due to objective lens hysteresis.
source: In order to prevent errors due to objective lens hysteresis the defocus was measured without applying a defocus offset during the measurement.
evidence: This describes a methodological choice to improve accuracy.

claim: The phase plate provides enough contrast for beam-tilt focus measurements even close to focus.
source: The phase plate provides enough contrast for beam-tilt focus measurements even close to focus.
evidence: This is based on the practical experience during data acquisition.

claim: Spherical aberration influences both the optimal defocus and the measured defocus.
source: Spherical aberration influences not only the optimal defocus but also the measured defocus.
evidence: This is based on the physics of electron optics and beam tilt focusing.

claim: The effect of spherical aberration on defocus measurement is usually ignored because its contribution is small compared to the typical defocus values used in CTEM.
source: The effect of spherical aberration on the measurement is usually ignored because its contribution is small compared to the typical defocus values used in CTEM.
evidence: This describes common practice in cryo-EM.

claim: Spherical aberration has an effect on defocus measurement equal to △z =CSβ2, where CS is the spherical aberration coefficient and β is the beam tilt angle.
source: Spherical aberration has an effect equal to a defocus of △z =CSβ2, where CS is the spherical aberraton coefficient and β is the beam tilt angle (Koster et al., 1987, equation 2).
evidence: This is a known relationship from electron optics theory, supported by citation.

claim: A 10 mrad beam tilt was used to improve the sensitivity of the measurement and to move the spots created on the VPP by the tilted beams further away from the central spot.
source: A commonly used tilt angle value is 5 mrad but in our experiments we used 10 mrad in order to improve the sensitivity of the measurement and to move the spots created on the VPP by the tilted beams further away from the central spot.
evidence: This describes a methodological choice in the experiments.

claim: On an FEI Titan Krios microscope, a 10 mrad beam tilt places the beam spot at a position corresponding to 5 nm-1 spatial frequency or 2 Å resolution.
source: On an FEI Titan Krios microscope (FEI, Hillsboro, OR) a 10 mrad beam tilt places the beam spot at a position corresponding to k = β /λ = 0.01 rad / 0.002 nm = 5 nm-1 spatial frequency or 2 Å resolution (λ is the electron wavelength).
evidence: This is calculated from the beam tilt angle and electron wavelength.

claim: Placing the tilted beam spots at high spatial frequency prevents the phase shifting spots created on the phase plate by the tilted beams from disturbing the CTF in the usable frequency range.
source: This prevents the phase shifting spots created on the phase plate by the tilted beams from disturbing the CTF in the usable frequency range.
evidence: This is an inference about the benefit of using larger beam tilt.

claim: The spots created by tilted beams on the phase plate act as phase plates themselves and increase the contrast of the tilted beam images, thus facilitating the measurement.
source: The spots themselves are beneficial for the focusing because they act as phase plates themselves and increase the contrast of the tilted beam images, thus facilitating the measurement.
evidence: This is an inference about the mechanism of contrast enhancement during focusing.

claim: The offset in the measured defocus caused by spherical aberration with 10 mrad beam tilt on an FEI Titan Krios is 270 nm.
source: The offset in the measured defocus caused by spherical aberration with 10 mrad beam tilt on an FEI Titan Krios is △z =CSβ 2 = 2.7 mm x 0.012 rad2 = 270 nm.
evidence: This is calculated from the spherical aberration coefficient and beam tilt angle.

claim: SerialEM software does not take into account the effect of spherical aberration on focus measurements.
source: We used SerialEM software (Mastronarde, 2005) for the data acquisition which does not take into account the effect of spherical aberration on focus measurements.
evidence: This is a statement about the capabilities of the software used.

claim: To get -20 nm actual defocus, the desired defocus had to be set at 250 nm in SerialEM to compensate for the 270 nm spherical aberration offset.
source: Therefore, we had to adjust the target defocus by the above offset, i.e. to get -20 nm actual defocus we had to set the desired defocus at 270 – 20 = 250 nm in the software.
evidence: This describes the correction applied during data acquisition.

claim: Phase shift measurements were performed under the same experimental conditions as those used to collect the 20S proteasome datasets.
source: In order to characterize the behavior of the VPP we measured the phase shift under the same experimental conditions as those used to collect the 20S proteasome datasets.
evidence: This describes the experimental methodology.

claim: Series of images were recorded automatically on carbon film parts of the sample with -1.5 μm defocus to facilitate phase shift measurement through CTF fitting.
source: Series of images were recorded automatically on carbon film parts of the sample with -1.5 μm defocus to facilitate phase shift measurement through CTF fitting.
evidence: This describes the experimental methodology.

claim: The CTFs of the image series were fitted with ctffind4 which supports phase shift.
source: The CTFs of the image series were fitted with the latest version of ctffind4 (Rohou and Grigorieff, 2015) which supports phase shift.
evidence: This describes the data analysis methodology.

claim: Two image series recorded at two consecutive positions on the VPP show very similar behavior indicating that there are no significant variations in performance between neighboring positions on the phase plate.
source: The results from two image series recorded at two consecutive positions on the VPP are plotted in Figure 3. Both series show very similar behavior indicating that there are no significant variations in performance between neighboring positions on the phase plate.
evidence: This is demonstrated by the data in Figure 3.

claim: The phase shift results reproduce well the previously reported VPP behavior.
source: The results reproduce well the previously reported VPP behavior (Danev et al., 2014, Figure 1B).
evidence: This is supported by comparison with cited previous work.

claim: During single particle data acquisition, the phase shift is prevented from going much over π/2 by periodically moving to a new position on the phase plate (every 25 to 50 images).
source: During single particle data acquisition we try to prevent the phase shift from going much over π/2 by periodically moving to a new position on the phase plate (depending on the experimental conditions, every 25 to 50 images).
evidence: This describes the data acquisition strategy used.

claim: Changing the phase plate position more often increases the risk of astigmatism due to variations in the phase plate film quality.
source: Changing the phase plate position more often increases the risk of astigmatism due to variations in the phase plate film quality.
evidence: This is an inference based on practical experience with the phase plate.

claim: It is desirable to have a phase plate with a slower rate of phase shift development.
source: Therefore, it is desirable to have a phase plate with a slower rate of phase shift development.
evidence: This is inferred from the need to balance phase shift control with minimizing position changes.

claim: The rate of phase shift development can be reduced by increasing the phase plate heating temperature.
source: In practice the rate can be reduced by increasing the phase plate heating temperature (Danev et al., 2014) but in the current VPP generation such control is quite limited by the specifications of the heater.
evidence: This is supported by citation to previous work on VPP operation.

claim: Two in-focus VPP datasets of the Thermoplasma acidophilum 20S proteasome were acquired, one at −20 nm and one at −50 nm defocus.
source: Using the acquisition scheme shown in Figure 2A we acquired two in-focus VPP datasets of the Thermoplasma acidophilum 20S proteasome, one at −20 nm and one at −50 nm defocus.
evidence: This describes the experimental datasets collected.

claim: A CTEM dataset with a defocus range of −0.8 to −1.7 um was acquired from the same grid square as the VPP datasets.
source: From the same grid square we also acquired a CTEM dataset with a defocus range of −0.8 to −1.7 um.
evidence: This describes the experimental datasets collected.

claim: The datasets were acquired automatically using SerialEM macros.
source: The datasets were acquired automatically using SerialEM macros (Mastronarde, 2005).
evidence: This describes the data acquisition methodology.

claim: The phase plate was automatically moved to a new area every ~1 hr (every ~27 images) to prevent too much phase shift buildup.
source: The phase plate was automatically moved to a new area every ~1 hr (every ~27 images) to prevent too much phase shift buildup.
evidence: This describes the data acquisition strategy.

claim: The VPP image has higher overall contrast compared to the CTEM image because of the improved low frequency transfer.
source: The VPP image (Figure 4A) has higher overall contrast compared to the CTEM image (Figure 4C) because of the improved low frequency transfer.
evidence: This is demonstrated by visual comparison of images in Figure 4.

claim: The high contrast provided by the VPP is very helpful during the particle picking process.
source: The high contrast is very helpful during the particle picking process.
evidence: This is an inference based on the improved visibility of particles.

claim: The VPP has a uniform transfer without visible CTF zeroes, with the first CTF zero beyond the 3.7 Å amorphous ice ring.
source: The VPP (Figure 4B) has a uniform transfer without visible zeroes. The first CTF zero is beyond the 3.7 Å amorphous ice ring and is not detectable in the transform.
evidence: This is demonstrated in Figure 4B power spectrum.

claim: The CTEM power spectrum shows characteristic CTF oscillations with multiple zeroes.
source: The spectrum of the CTEM image (Figure 4D) shows characteristic CTF oscillations with multiple zeroes.
evidence: This is demonstrated in Figure 4D power spectrum.

claim: Both VPP and CTEM power spectra exhibit a noticeable amplitude decrease in their central region which is a consequence of the relatively high dose rate on the detector (~9 e-/pixel/s).
source: Both power spectra exhibit a noticeable amplitude decrease in their central region which is a consequence of the relatively high dose rate on the detector (~9 e-/pixel/s).
evidence: This is inferred from known detector behavior at high dose rates, supported by citation.

claim: Higher dose rates increase the coincidence loss during electron counting and lead to amplitude reduction at low spatial frequencies but have little effect on the spectral signal-to-noise ratio.
source: Higher dose rates increase the coincidence loss during electron counting and lead to amplitude reduction at low spatial frequencies but have little effect on the spectral signal-to-noise ratio (Li et al., 2013b).
evidence: This is supported by citation to work on detector performance.

claim: The reconstruction from the -20 nm defocus VPP dataset is based on 13,469 particles selected after a 3D classification step from an initial dataset of 35,469 particles.
source: The reconstruction is based on 13,469 particles selected after a 3D classification step from an initial dataset of 35,469 particles.
evidence: This describes the data processing methodology.

claim: The density map shows the presence of side chain densities.
source: Figure 5B shows a part of the map superposed on an α-helix from the β subunit of a 20S atomic model (PDB 3J9I) and demonstrates the presence of side chain densities.
evidence: This is demonstrated in Figure 5B.

claim: Both the 'gold standard' FSC and the external map FSC give an identical resolution estimate of 3.2 Å.
source: Both criteria give an identical resolution estimate of 3.2 Å at 0.143 level for the 'gold standard' FSC and at 0.5 level for the external map FSC.
evidence: This is shown in Figure 5C FSC curves.

claim: The 3.2 Å resolution is the highest resolution phase plate single particle reconstruction reported to date.
source: This is the highest resolution phase plate single particle reconstruction reported to date.
evidence: This is a comparative statement based on the literature at the time of publication.

claim: Both the VPP and the CTEM show a gradual improvement of resolution as the number of particles increases with the performance being virtually identical between the two techniques.
source: Both the VPP and the CTEM show a gradual improvement of resolution as the number of particles increases with the performance being virtually identical between the two techniques.
evidence: This is demonstrated in Figure 6A.

claim: The conventional dataset contained more micrographs (293 vs 158) and had more particles (after 3D classification, 35,717 vs 13,469) than the VPP dataset.
source: The conventional dataset contained more micrographs (293 vs 158) hence it had more particles (after 3D classification, 35,717 vs 13,469).
evidence: This describes the composition of the datasets.

claim: With more than twice the number of particles, the CTEM dataset reached a resolution of 3.1 Å.
source: With more than twice the number of particles the CTEM dataset reached a resolution of 3.1 Å.
evidence: This is based on the data processing results.

claim: The measured B-factors in Relion were very similar between the two datasets: 119 for CTEM and 123 for VPP.
source: The measured B-factors in Relion were very similar between the two datasets: 119 for CTEM and 123 for VPP.
evidence: This is based on the Relion software output.

claim: The region with particle numbers between 500 and 2000 has a B-factor of ~100 and resolutions above 3.6 Å.
source: The region with particle numbers between 500 and 2000 has a B-factor of ~100 and resolutions above 3.6 Å (solid lines in Figure 6B).
evidence: This is derived from linear fits to the data in Figure 6B.

claim: The higher resolution region with particle numbers above 2000 has a B-factor of ~200.
source: The higher resolution region with particle numbers above 2000 has a B-factor of ~200 (dashed lines in Figure 6B).
evidence: This is derived from linear fits to the data in Figure 6B.

claim: A VPP dataset collected at -50 nm defocus consisting of 6340 particles reached a resolution of 3.5 Å which is marginally (0.2 Å) worse than the same number of particles from the -20 nm defocus VPP dataset.
source: A VPP dataset collected at -50 nm defocus and consisting of 6340 particles reached a resolution of 3.5 Å which is marginally (0.2 Å) worse than the same number of particles from the -20 nm defocus VPP dataset.
evidence: This is shown in Figure 6A and based on data processing results.

claim: According to the phase shift values and CTF curves, the -50 nm defocus dataset should have matched or exceeded the performance of the -20 nm defocus dataset.
source: According to the values of the phase shift in Figure 3 and comparing them with the curves in Figure 1C the -50 nm defocus dataset should have matched or exceeded the performance of the -20 nm defocus dataset.
evidence: This is an inference based on theoretical predictions from Figures 1C and 3.

claim: The slightly worse performance of the -50 nm dataset suggests that either there was a small systematic focusing error or a variation in the phase plate performance.
source: This would suggest that either there was a small systematic focusing error or a variation in the phase plate performance.
evidence: This is speculation about possible causes of the observed difference.

claim: A VPP dataset collected on an FEI Tecnai F20 microscope equipped with an FEI Falcon II direct detector reached a resolution of 4.5 Å.
